source: Detailed CEN 04/2026 (JE/DMS, with Corrigendum-1 adding CMA), published on the official RRB websites on 13-08-2026: https://rrb.indianrailways.gov.in/-/image/1787058904504CEN_04_2026_JE_DMS_English.pdf/examsDocuments
intro: CBT 1 is a common screening paper of Mathematics, General Intelligence and Reasoning, General Awareness and General Science. CBT 2 adds Physics and Chemistry, computers and environment to the common blocks, plus 100 questions from your engineering branch (Exam Group).
note: In the CBT 1 paper General Science and General Awareness are separate blocks: General Science carries 30 questions and General Awareness 15 (the CEN marks both splits as indicative).

sections.name: General Science and General Awareness
topics: General Science: Physics (up to 10th standard CBSE)
General Science: Chemistry (up to 10th standard CBSE)
General Science: Life Sciences (up to 10th standard CBSE)
Culture and history of India including the freedom struggle
Environmental issues concerning India and the world
sections.tip: General Science carries 30 questions against 15 for General Awareness in CBT 1, so the 10th-standard science parts deserve more preparation time.

sections.name: General Awareness
topics: Same scope as CBT 1 General Awareness (15 questions)

sections.name: Physics and Chemistry
topics: Physics and Chemistry up to 10th standard CBSE (15 questions)

sections.name: Basics of Computers and Applications
topics: Operating systems like Windows, Unix, Linux
sections.tip: This block carries 10 questions in CBT 2, along with 10 more from Basics of Environment and Pollution Control, so the site's computer practice covers both well.

sections.name: Basics of Environment and Pollution Control
topics: Adverse effects of environmental pollution and control strategies
Air, water and noise pollution, their effects and control

sections.name: Technical Abilities (Exam Group)
topics: Mechanical and Allied Engineering (Annexure VIII-A): engineering mechanics, material science, strength of materials, machining, welding, grinding and finishing, metrology, fluid mechanics and hydraulic machinery, industrial management, thermal engineering and allied topics

Electrical and Allied Engineering (Annexure VIII-B): basic concepts, circuit laws, magnetic circuits, AC fundamentals, measurement and measuring instruments, electrical machines, synchronous machines, generation, transmission and distribution, estimation and costing, utilisation of electrical energy, basic electronics

Electronics and Allied Engineering (Annexure VIII-C): electronic components and materials, electronic devices and circuits, digital electronics, linear integrated circuits, microprocessor and microcontroller, electronic measurements, communication engineering, data communication and networks, computer programming, basic electrical engineering

Civil and Allied Engineering (Annexure VIII-D): engineering mechanics, building construction and materials, substructure and superstructure, building finishes, maintenance and drawing, concrete technology, surveying, CAD, geotechnical engineering, hydraulics, irrigation engineering, mechanics of structures, theory of structures, design of concrete and steel structures, transportation (railway and highway) engineering, environmental engineering, advanced construction techniques, estimating and costing, contracts and accounts

CMA group (Annexure VIII-E, for Chemical & Metallurgical Assistant): measurements, units and dimensions; light, heat, sound, mechanics, magnetism, electricity and electromagnetism, modern physics, electronics and communications; matter, chemical reactions, acids, bases and salts, atomic structure, periodic classification, chemical bonding, carbon and its compounds and allied Chemistry topics
sections.tip: 100 of the 150 CBT 2 questions come from your Exam Group, so this is the block that decides the merit list.
